original_question: Let X be a cubic threefold. If sigma is any stability condition on the Kuznetsov component Ku(X), is sigma in the same orbit as the explicitly constructed stability conditions sigma(s, q, mu)? Equivalently, is every stability condition on Ku(X) Serre-invariant?
target_in_paper: Question 6.25 in Section 6.4 ("Cubic threefolds: applications"), motivated by Remark 6.24: "Let sigma be a stability condition on Ku(X) of a cubic threefold X. Is sigma in the same orbit of sigma(s,q,mu)? Equivalently, is sigma Serre-invariant?"
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's exact open problem almost verbatim. It has the right object (the Kuznetsov component Ku(X) of a cubic threefold), the right family of reference stability conditions sigma(s,q,mu), the right orbit question, and the paper's own equivalent reformulation in terms of Serre-invariance.
missing_details: The paper is working with a smooth cubic threefold X ⊂ P^4, not an arbitrary possibly singular cubic threefold.

In the relevant part of the paper (Section 6.4, continuing the standing assumption after equation (6.7)), the ground field is C; the authors note just before Theorem 6.18 that the same proof should apply more generally over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, but the official discussion here is over C.
The phrase "stability condition" should be made explicit as a Bridgeland stability condition on the triangulated category Ku(X).
Ku(X) should be defined stand-alone as the Kuznetsov component Ku(X) := ⟨O_X, O_X(H_X)⟩^⊥ ⊂ D^b(X), where H_X is the hyperplane class.
The orbit must be identified as the orbit under the standard action of the universal cover of GL_2^+(R) on the stability manifold.
The notation sigma(s,q,mu) should be tied to Theorem 6.17 and equation (6.7), not just called "explicitly constructed".
The admissible parameter range for sigma(s,q,mu) should be stated: (s,q) ∈ Delta := {(s,q) ∈ R^2 : q > (1/2)s^2}, q < -(1/2)s, and mu_{s,q}(O_X(-H_X)[1]) <= mu < mu_{s,q}(O_X).
Because many sigma(s,q,mu) occur, the question should say "the same orbit as one, equivalently any, admissible sigma(s,q,mu)" to remove ambiguity.
If the equivalent formulation is used, "Serre-invariant" should be defined as in Definition 6.11: S_{Ku(X)}·sigma lies in the same universal-cover-GL_2^+(R) orbit as sigma.

The equivalence between the orbit formulation and the Serre-invariance formulation is not merely terminological; nearby results show it using Theorem 6.18 together with the uniqueness of the orbit of Serre-invariant stability conditions from Corollary 6.21.
refined_question: Let X ⊂ P^4 be a smooth cubic threefold over C, let H_X denote the hyperplane class, and let Ku(X) := ⟨O_X, O_X(H_X)⟩^⊥ ⊂ D^b(X) be its Kuznetsov component. For admissible real parameters (s,q,mu) with (s,q) in Delta := {(s,q) in R^2 : q > (1/2)s^2}, q < -(1/2)s, and mu_{s,q}(O_X(-H_X)[1]) <= mu < mu_{s,q}(O_X), let sigma(s,q,mu) be the Bridgeland stability condition on Ku(X) constructed in Theorem 6.17 and equation (6.7). Is every Bridgeland stability condition sigma on Ku(X) in the same orbit, under the standard action of the universal cover of GL_2^+(R), as one (equivalently any) such sigma(s,q,mu)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, is every Bridgeland stability condition sigma on Ku(X) Serre-invariant in the sense of Definition 6.11; that is, does there exist an element of the universal cover of GL_2^+(R) such that S_{Ku(X)}·sigma = sigma·g̃?
justification: The draft clearly targets Question 6.25 in Section 6.4, not a broader neighboring problem. The notation sigma(s,q,mu) is introduced in Theorem 6.17 and equation (6.7), after Definition 6.11 gives the notion of Serre-invariance. Theorem 6.18 proves that any stability condition in the orbit of sigma(s,q,mu) is Serre-invariant, Corollary 6.21 gives uniqueness of the orbit of Serre-invariant stability conditions for Ku(X), and Corollary 6.23 together with Remark 6.24 explain that all known stability conditions on Ku(X) are already in that same orbit. Question 6.25 then asks whether this exhausts all stability conditions on Ku(X).
